title: Audit of the wave-pinning crawler's front repair (IMR): it replicates on fresh seeds 5-6 and at dt/2, but the repaired cell stays at 66% of its twin's area for good, because size is set by total conserved protein. With the erased protein kept in the cell, it regrows to full size within 2 t. R is the reorganization of the remaining material, not the replacement of lost matter
summary: Construction: world.py is Camley et al.'s crawler. The phase field moves by (rho - rho*)|grad phi| plus Allen-Cahn curvature flow, which is not area-preserving, so area is set by protrusion against shrinkage. The polarity protein is mass-conserved, with bistable kinetics and one well-mixed cytosolic pool per body. Nothing produces protein. The cut zeroes phi and rho in a 30% sector at the leading edge, and the erased protein leaves the cell. Replication, labkit packs of world.py on seeds 5 and 6 (pack_front with cut_t=8, cut_mode front; pack_twin without): one crawler per run, 91/91 frames; cut cells travel 3.7/3.3 body lengths, twins 4.6/4.6. Side-by-side cut runs (the author's cutrun.py): seed 5 and seed 6 cut 26-27% of the area and 31-32% of the protein. The front splits into two lateral domains, the cell becomes a dumbbell, one domain wins by t~11-12 and the cell crawls on as a single-front half-moon at 0.384/0.385 vs twin 0.421/0.418. A real dt/2 (world dt 5e-4, seed 6) gives the same (0.417 vs 0.453, area 1.75 vs 2.65). Area after the cut: 1.73-1.75 at t=13-18 on every seed, against 2.61-2.65 for the twin, and it even falls from 1.92 just after the cut. Deciding control (world_keep.py, keep_protein=1: the same cut, but the erased protein stays in the remaining cell's cytosolic pool; seed 5): the cell regrows to area 2.62 by t=10 and crawls at 0.421, exactly the twin's 2.63 and 0.421 (cuts/s5_front30_keep/cut.png).

observations.I: pack_front/seed5/FACTS.md: one body, 91/91 frames, alive start to end
observations.M: pack_twin/seed5, seed6 FACTS: 4.6 body lengths in 18 t; cut cells 3.7 and 3.3
observations.R: cuts/s5_front30/cut.png, cuts/s6_front30/cut.png: after a 26-27% front cut the split polarity resolves into one front by t~11-12 and the cell crawls on at 0.384-0.385 vs twin 0.418-0.421; dt/2 (cuts/s6_front30_dt2) the same

controls_run.R: pack_twin/seed5, seed6 and the twin arms of cuts/s5_front30, s6_front30 (undamaged, branched at t=8); cuts/s5_front30_keep (world_keep.py: erased protein kept in the cell's pool): full regrowth to the twin's area and speed, showing the permanent 34% size deficit in the claimed world is set by the conserved protein total

verdicts.limitation: R is reorganization only. The polarity comes back to one front (winner-take-all of wave-pinned domains through the shared pool, Mori et al. 2008). The cell never replaces lost matter: it lives on at 66% of its area and ~91% of its speed, because nothing makes protein and the area window is set by the protein total. The keep-protein control proves this; it breaks the rule that erased matter must leave, so it is a control and not R evidence. Repair needs a surviving polarity domain (the author's polarity-erase arm is fatal). Planted cell, one per run. I did not re-run the linear twin. The post-cut speed spike (0.8-0.9 at t~11) is the dumbbell snapping back, not crawling.
